import os

TOKEN = os.environ['APP_API_TOKEN']
TOKEN_TTL = int(os.environ.get('APP_TOKEN_TTL', '3600'))

# Configuration
| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| APP_API_TOKEN | API token |
| APP_TOKEN_TTL | Token lifetime in seconds |
| LOG_LEVEL | Log verbosity |

report: These are proposals only: nothing was applied and no tests were run. The change renames the exact variable APP_TOKEN to APP_API_TOKEN in deploy/env.example. It also updates the two workspace files that read that name, src/settings.py (required os.environ lookup) and scripts/check_env.sh (the ${...:?missing} guard), plus the docs table in docs/config.md. Without those consumer updates the app and the check script would fail once the new example is used. APP_TOKEN_TTL is a different variable that only shares a prefix with the old name, so it is left as is in every file, and LOG_LEVEL is unchanged. I did not add a fallback to the old name: no requirement or design asks for one, and the method says a retained compatibility mechanism needs a stated reason. The remaining risk is any deployed environment outside this workspace that still sets only APP_TOKEN. After this change it would fail at startup or in check_env.sh, so it must set APP_API_TOKEN.
